key_facts.fact_en: Price AED 136,500 with a warranty of 3 years or 100,000 km; bought and delivered on 16 Jun 2026, after 1 June 2026, so the 2025 Civil Transactions Law governs the sale

First repair under warranty, job card JC-2026-04417 (28 Jul 2026, 3,184 km): judder on pulling away, late shift from second to third gear and a gearbox warning; diagnosis, control-unit software update, valve body and gearbox oil replaced; car returned 8 Aug 2026 at no charge
The technician's handwritten findings: third-gear clutch slipping and gearbox oil overheating, 'manufacturing defect'
The same fault returned and the car was repaired again on 24 Aug 2026, with the control unit replaced; this appears only in the technician's handwriting on the same job card
The gearbox failed a third time on 6 Oct 2026; no job card for this visit is in the file
The dealer refused replacement or refund on 13 Oct 2026, and never provided a replacement car

reader_should_flag: Article 45 of the Consumer Protection Law does not exist (the law has 38 articles). It is cited for the dealer's burden of proving misuse.
The date of the second repair (24 Aug 2026) appears only in the technician's handwritten note on the job card; the statement of claim mentions the second repair without a date.
The technician's handwritten finding calls the gearbox fault a manufacturing defect; this admission is in handwriting only.

Article 13 needs the same fault three times within the first year after delivery. The file shows the first repair (28 Jul 2026, printed job card), the second (24 Aug 2026, handwriting only) and the third failure (6 Oct 2026, stated only in the claim, with no job card in the file).

The car was bought and delivered on 16 Jun 2026, after 1 June 2026, so the sale falls under the 2025 Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025), which the claim cites, not the 1985 law.
The 36 days of car hire (AED 7,920) are not broken down; the file documents only the first workshop stay (28 Jul to 8 Aug 2026).
